purpose: Security boundaries for AI prompts, retrieved context, model outputs and tool execution across Shine applications.
requirements: Trusted application instructions remain separate from untrusted user, retrieved, uploaded and external content.
Prompt construction marks user, memory, retrieval, document and provider content as data rather than authority.
Only the minimum personal or confidential context required for the task is sent to a model or tool.
Provider storage is disabled when the provider and feature support a no-storage mode for private Shine interactions.
Model requests and responses use deadlines and bounded sizes before parsing or persistence.
Structured model outputs are schema-validated and fail closed when malformed, incomplete or outside the expected contract.
Model-generated URLs, file paths, identifiers and tool arguments are validated by application policy before use.
Tools and side-effecting actions use explicit allowlists and least privilege; model text cannot bypass authentication, authorisation or ownership checks.
High-impact or irreversible actions require deterministic application checks and any human confirmation required by the product flow.
Retrieved memories, documents, provider results and prior AI output preserve provenance so generated text does not silently become authoritative stored fact.
Secrets and service credentials are not intentionally placed in model prompts, model-visible logs or user-visible model output.
AI failures and uncertain outputs remain explicit; applications do not silently fabricate successful tool execution or verified facts.
Security-relevant AI and tool events can be audited without logging raw secrets or unnecessary private prompt content.
nonClaims: This policy does not guarantee model output is factually correct.
This policy does not eliminate prompt injection or model error.
This policy does not make an AI model an authorisation system.
This policy does not certify autonomous high-impact actions without separately proven safeguards.
